subject: PHI deployment paths & BAA intake — next steps

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: PHI deployment paths & BAA intake — next steps

Hi Lisa / Jacob —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the compliance questions you raised.

Key takeaways from discussion:
- BAA: Redwood can execute a Business Associate Agreement. BAAs are standard for Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. Hosted (shared multi-tenant) is not eligible for PHI under our standard terms.
- PHI handling boundaries: PHI workloads must run on Dedicated with contractual isolation + BAA or on Private deployments (VPC or on-prem). We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments.
- SOC 2: We can share our latest SOC 2 Type II summary and will provide the full report under an NDA / secure link.
- Data retention & logs: Default telemetry/log retention can be shortened or routed to customer storage in Private deployments; we can provide specifics once we see your retention window requirements.
- Vendor questionnaire: I attached a completed vendor questionnaire template for your team to review (vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx). Please flag any unanswered items and we’ll have security respond.

Action items / next steps:
1) You: confirm the primary PHI use cases (inbound PHI ingestion, embeddings storage, transient inference only) so we can validate the right deployment path.
2) Redwood: share SOC 2 summary + sample BAA draft (attached) and have Security/Legal perform a focused Q&A on items you highlight in the questionnaire.
3) Proposed follow-up: 45-minute security deep-dive with our Security + Solutions Engineers. Availability next week?

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx, redwood_sample_baa_draft.pdf

Thanks — I’ll loop Stephanie from Security once you confirm the questionnaire items you want answered.

Best,
Karthik Iyer

Thanks Karthik — helpful summary. A few clarifying items from our side so we can scope the security call: 

1) PHI patterns: our initial plan is to ingest structured clinical notes (name, dob, mrn, diagnosis codes) and generate redacted summaries. Do you support on-the-fly tokenization or do you expect customers to de-identify prior to sending?
2) Embeddings & storage: will embeddings derived from PHI be stored by Redwood by default? Can we opt out or request zero-retention for embeddings in Dedicated/Private?
3) Network isolation and audit: for Dedicated deployments, what controls do you provide for VPC peering, private endpoints, and audit log export (SIEM integration)?
4) Timeline: how long does your legal/ops team typically take to sign a BAA and provision a Dedicated environment once terms are agreed?

We’ll review the questionnaire and highlight any high-risk answers. For the security deep-dive, Jacob and I are available Tuesday/Wednesday next week after 10am PT.

Hi all — Stephanie from Security. Thanks for the clear list, Karthik / Lisa. Quick answers below to prep for the security deep-dive; happy to expand on any item during the call.

1) Tokenization / de-identification: Redwood does not perform automatic de-identification on customer payloads in Hosted. We recommend customers de-identify prior to sending where feasible. For Dedicated/Private, customers can deploy preprocessing agents in their VPC/on-prem to perform tokenization or de-id prior to hitting the inference endpoints. We can share reference patterns and an SDK example.

2) Embeddings retention: By default embeddings are persisted for feature caches and to support downstream tooling. For Dedicated and Private, retention can be configured to zero or routed to customer-managed storage; we also support an option to disable persistent storage of embeddings. We will document the exact API/config toggles for the call.

3) Network isolation / audit: Dedicated supports private endpoints, VPC peering, and IP allowlists. Audit logs (access, admin actions, model / prompt tracing) can be exported to your SIEM via secure syslog or pushed to a customer bucket. For Private on-prem, everything stays inside your network subject to your controls.

4) Timeline for BAA + provisioning: Typical turnaround is 2–4 weeks for legal review on a standard BAA. Provisioning a Dedicated environment after contracts are signed is usually 3–7 business days; Private/VPC deployments can take 2–4 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS integration. We’ll surface any exceptions during the legal review.

Attachments / links: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (link shared to your secure folder), redwood_sample_baa_draft.pdf

Next steps:
- Lisa / Jacob: mark the questionnaire items you want answered in priority order; we’ll close high-risk items before the call.
- Karthik / Vanessa: propose two time slots for the call; I’ll bring the engineer who owns KMS and the audit export pipeline.

See you on the call —
Stephanie Nguyen
